question: How do machine unlearning methods perform? Can they be used to remove knowledge from language models?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: Defines machine unlearning as transforming a trained model so it behaves as if it had never been trained on certain data.
examples: The goal is to make the model behave as though the forget data was never included in training.
Unlearning transforms an already-trained model into one indistinguishable from one retrained without the target data.

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: Describes TOFU as a benchmark for fictitious unlearning with 200 synthetic author profiles, 20 QA pairs each, a designated forget set, and holistic metrics plus baseline results.
examples: TOFU provides 200 synthetic author profiles, each with 20 QA pairs, and a forget set targeted for unlearning.
The TOFU benchmark includes holistic metrics and baseline results for unlearning efficacy.

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: Reports that none of the baseline algorithms evaluated in TOFU achieve effective unlearning, motivating further research.
examples: None of the baseline unlearning algorithms in TOFU showed effective unlearning.
No baseline behaves as if never trained on the forget data, motivating new approaches.

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: Identifies MUSE as a comprehensive benchmark evaluating unlearning across six properties: no verbatim memorization, no knowledge memorization, no privacy leakage, utility preservation, scalability, and sustainability.
examples: MUSE evaluates six properties: no verbatim memorization, no knowledge memorization, no privacy leakage, utility preservation, scalability, and sustainability over sequential requests.
MUSE is a six-way evaluation framework assessing unlearning from both deployer and data owner perspectives.

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: States that most of the eight benchmarked algorithms can prevent verbatim and knowledge memorization to varying degrees, showing partial success at knowledge removal.
examples: Most algorithms prevent verbatim and knowledge memorization to some degree.
Several of the eight algorithms partially succeed at removing memorized content.

ingredients.name: answer_critical_5
ingredients.criterion: States that only one algorithm avoids severe privacy leakage, that existing algorithms degrade general utility, and that they cannot sustainably handle successive or large-scale unlearning requests.
examples: Only one algorithm does not lead to severe privacy leakage; most degrade utility and fail to scale.
Algorithms cannot handle successive removal requests or large removal requests.

ingredients.name: answer_critical_6
ingredients.criterion: Concludes with a direct answer: current machine unlearning methods cannot effectively remove knowledge from language models without significantly compromising overall utility.
examples: Overall, current unlearning methods cannot remove knowledge without significantly compromising model utility.
The answer is largely no: effective, utility-preserving unlearning of LLMs remains unsolved.

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: Mentions that MUSE benchmarks eight popular unlearning algorithms on 7B-parameter language models using real-world corpora such as Harry Potter books and news articles, contrasting with TOFU's synthetic setting.
examples: MUSE tests eight algorithms on 7B-parameter LMs with Harry Potter books and news articles.
Unlike TOFU's synthetic profiles, MUSE benchmarks on real copyrighted text, giving complementary evidence.

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: Notes that prior evaluation of unlearning algorithms was narrow in scope, failing to quantify success and practicality from both model deployer and data owner perspectives, motivating these benchmarks.
examples: Prior evaluations were narrow, prompting MUSE's comprehensive six-way framework.
TOFU was created to deepen understanding of unlearning, an underexplored challenge.

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: Highlights the trade-off both benchmarks reveal between removing target knowledge and preserving utility on retained data.
examples: Both benchmarks reveal the trade-off between removing target knowledge and preserving retained utility.
TOFU and MUSE offer complementary perspectives on efficacy vs practicality of unlearning.
